2f861a13-03da-4644-b0f2-17c42f04c221.notes: Hi, I'm Viviana matsuda. Um, I do pottery for a living. My brand name is Mud Witch. Um, yeah. I'm a full time potter.

43deb348-7ffa-40cd-8b88-321e548726f7.notes: Um, so my voice and style for mud, which it's kind of a funny thing where when I was learning to do ceramics, I was also learning about the body positivity movement.

6a9d8e5b-77eb-4d5c-85e8-0dfd61a6ada1.notes: first times like seeing different types of different shapes of bodies. I think that that kind of just smushed into one. And I was like starting to make these like chubby shapes and they're literally called this is the Chubby Mug. This is the Venus mug because I think those two things kind of just mushed together the learning clay and the body positivity. Um, and so they were originally supposed to be kind of like an abstract like vision of, of people, like different bodies sitting, dancing, whatever.

e693651c-25b6-4824-9028-c8bed65e739d.notes: I think those two things kind of just mushed together the learning clay and the body positivity.

a3e6bf07-6559-49c7-a5e9-96e2b2aba876.notes: I, It started off as one thing, and now it's just like, I just want to make something that, like, makes people smile.

a3f4a261-6d42-4035-a864-8b1897bddf90.notes: I think physical mediums are so important because, um, it's a way of connecting.

673dddc1-6544-41f8-94b3-2bfea27776a5.notes: and I think that that is very important because we, you know, in society, we're like, so becoming more and more disconnected to, like human interaction in especially, like, touch or anything along those lines.

87803fe6-3da2-49a8-bcdf-3b27a51e2ad9.notes: with lockdown, people really sat in their houses and realized that the things that were surrounding them weren't bringing them joy. And I think that's why ceramics has had such a big surge.

b3793efd-09ba-4d22-87b0-6880a679192a.notes: But not only that, but like, you don't need all of that stuff. Like, you could literally just get a couple things that make you happy.

e3bc8a87-5c11-4e08-8466-e8e19e654adf.notes: better view of her using tools

narrative.text:
## Creative brief
Plan a ~60-second documentary about how Viviana turned her pottery into Mud Witch and why she values pottery.

## Overview & Tone

This 60-second piece is an intimate, tactile profile of ceramicist Viviana Matsuda and the ethos behind Mud Witch. The tone is warm, grounded, and meditative, built on an inviting bed of continuous dreamy, upbeat music (`dreamy_upbeat.wav`) [node: card_91c0234e-109c-42f4-85d6-528fc58d9fc9]. Visually, the edit transitions smoothly from personal introductory talking heads to rich, sensory b-roll of spinning clay and finished ceramics, culminating in a reflective message about mindful living and finding joy in simple, handmade things.

---

## Story Beats

#### 1. Introduction to Mud Witch (0:00–0:11) [node: beat_39cb4f5e-f7b9-4fbd-b647-01e84e593748]

We open cold on Viviana’s clean, direct on-camera sync introduction from `A001C002_240718OR` (14.99s–25s) [node: card_ed9128ad-6ee3-4fe7-ad53-b2910160bdab] (A001C002_240718OR (14.996487008616777s–25s)), where she introduces herself, explains that pottery is her full-time craft, and announces her brand name, Mud Witch [node: card_e98de4c8-6bee-44a6-81e7-e534465f4c8d]. To anchor her in her physical environment right away, we cut on her mention of "Mud Witch" at around the 4.3-second mark to exterior storefront b-roll `B003C009_240719KG` (16s–20.3s) [node: card_f6662114-13fc-4079-83e4-537a1c2e5613] (B003C009_240719KG (16s–20.3s)), letting her dialogue continue underneath as audio [node: card_9696a9dd-704c-452a-bf62-aa9cf3635cfb]. 

#### 2. Developing Style and Voice (0:11–0:24) [node: beat_ef5361be-1b82-4578-b133-533dcd9708e3]

Here we transition into Viviana’s artistic evolution and brand identity [node: card_10c95065-7d58-4484-95bd-622ca8892070]. Using the select sequence from interview group [node: card_97cf1fa2-48e6-4b40-bb47-9c34a1508bdb] (A001C004_240718BC (668.9s–682.5s); A001C004_240718BC (682.6s–693.9s))—prioritizing the tighter take in `A001C004_240718BC` (668.9s–682.5s) to establish how she discovered her voice [node: card_9bf07ff0-23bc-4f3d-992b-1e359fb89897] while holding the later take `A001C004_240718BC` (682.6s–693.9s) as an alternative bridge into her artistic expression [node: card_e3abcef1-507a-449e-916c-5f1abca25882]—the story expands into what makes her aesthetic unique. Visually, her voiceover is supported by seamless cutaways: first to a warm shelf shot featuring the Mud Witch sign from `B003C028_240719CX` (11.3s–13.6s) [node: card_c5cdf7a4-61f1-47f1-b5ba-30883a9e8120] (B003C028_240719CX (11.3s–13.6s)) [node: card_03f5951e-bab9-484b-8334-7cb2efb82182], immediately followed by macro detail of her finished ceramic pieces on display from `B003C011_240719YX` (5.9s–9.1s) [node: card_e54ace40-7016-4d08-aeb9-a94f20c9e403] (B003C011_240719YX (5.9s–9.1s)) [node: card_28e93c0f-ee7b-4955-9938-440e4a636b1f].

#### 3. Craft and Daily Dedication (0:24–0:46) [node: beat_93f4b549-4948-43c2-9066-85da2afcb59c]

This beat dives into the physical, meditative process of pottery and her daily dedication to the wheel [node: card_486d0c13-a5e1-429f-97b6-b72a69c1b2f1]. On the A-roll side, we weave together trimmed interview reflections from group [node: card_c1b16f25-3a81-49fc-b57a-9d166ceaf849] (A001C004_240718BC (702.3s–707.8s); A001C004_240718BC (756s–762s); A001C004_240718BC (892.3s–897.1s); A001C004_240718BC (907.1s–923.6s)) to articulate why she loves what she does [node: card_7c9b111e-3390-4447-8c7f-7de06577544b], [node: card_93f9526f-d1bc-407f-8ece-903a8c11609d]. We cut between the focused soundbites in `A001C004_240718BC` (702.3s–707.8s) and `A001C004_240718BC` (756s–762s), while using the best soundbite section trimmed down from `A001C004_240718BC` (907.1s–923.6s) to eliminate dead air, leaving `A001C004_240718BC` (892.3s–897.1s) unused as an extraneous take. 

Over this dialogue, we build a rhythmic montage of studio b-roll [node: card_9b446ae2-055e-442a-8596-0c96a36d044d] pulling from group [node: card_10590ac4-70e2-4efa-be5e-4da036a7eb69] (B003C006_240719KM (42.6s–52.4s); B003C007_240719CC (34.2s–39.8s); B003C050_240719XK (9.6s–14.2s)): opening on tactile clay throwing in `B003C006_240719KM` (42.6s–52.4s), cutting to hands shaping forms on the wheel in `B003C007_240719CC` (34.2s–39.8s) [node: card_bf010ae6-d961-4235-8e14-de5797eb3587], and landing on the vibrant glaze details of finished mugs in `B003C050_240719XK` (9.6s–14.2s) [node: card_346e90ba-8b0c-43d1-aeeb-cb53203dd077].

#### 4. Value, Simplicity, and Outro (0:46–1:00) [node: beat_6f583a76-db11-450d-aafd-be56479e4796]

The final movement resolves Viviana’s artistic philosophy on conscious consumption and finding joy in handcrafted objects [node: card_fa3c2c83-ec44-4fdb-bb74-2c0917643114]. From the A-roll interview group [node: card_d5a8bcab-8a11-4e61-b9a3-ae4b3d47bd19] (A001C004_240718BC (1209.2s–1221.1s); A001C004_240718BC (1257.6s–1263.8s)), we introduce her reflection on consumer habits with `A001C004_240718BC` (1209.2s–1221.1s) [node: card_8acdbea2-6447-4b3b-b4aa-84786494633e] and transition seamlessly into her standout takeaway line from `A001C004_240718BC` (1257.6s–1263.8s): “You don't need all of that stuff. Like, you could literally just get a couple things that make you happy” [node: card_a2cb8062-1e5b-4a3c-92e7-57a1d1f465b9].

Visual coverage pulls from group [node: card_4d5f3376-9b93-4aab-be64-96836384ad93] (B003C050_240719XK (29.2s–33.9s); B003C061_240719AN (6.5s–13.6s)), showing warm studio shelves with `B003C050_240719XK` (29.2s–33.9s) [node: card_a0be346f-3b84-4814-ad3c-bbdbae016fb9], before cutting to the exterior tracking shot of Viviana walking out of the studio in `B003C061_240719AN` (6.5s–13.6s) [node: card_811d428b-f994-4d56-af2f-83eb40bfc407]. As she walks into the distance, a minimal graphic title reading "Mudwitch" appears on screen [node: card_9c63547c-285c-4e83-908f-a6507a79e6fd] as the music gently fades out to black.

## Constraints

- The plan above is the spec — it already made the editorial calls (what to use, what to omit, how to sequence and combine material). Follow the plan's own decisions rather than independently re-deriving them from first principles.
- Track is authoritative for whatever the plan places on a given track. A shot the plan describes as A-Roll must land on the A-Roll track, B-Roll on B-Roll, music on the Music track, and text/graphics on the Text/Graphics track. A card does not count as fulfilled merely because related material appears elsewhere in the timeline on the wrong track.
- Timecodes and durations in the plan are approximate targets, not exact requirements — use editorial judgment on the actual cut points, same as any real edit.
- A Music card whose source names a real file path (marked "real stock audio file") must be added directly with `edit-timeline add-clip <path> --row music --role music` — do not call `/generate music` for it.

## Instructions for tagging

When adding a clip with `edit-timeline add-clip`, attach the corresponding plan node ID using `--node-ids card_<id>` (or `beat_<id>` for a beat-level marker).

If one clip fulfills multiple plan node ids, include all applicable ones.

Only attach a node ID when the clip actually fulfills what the plan describes for it, including its named track. Use the exact node IDs from the plan. Do not invent or modify them.

## Completion requirements

Before finishing, verify against the plan's own decisions, not the original grid.

For each beat, confirm the edit the plan describes was actually realized: the right material landed on the right track, in the intended order, with any transitions/overlaps the plan called out.

For any node id the plan itself named as an intentionally unused alternative or backup, no further action is needed — that was already the plan's own decision, not something to silently reconsider or silently include anyway.

A node id that the plan actively describes using, but that never lands on the corresponding clip, is a real gap — note it and the reason in verification.

### Beat 1: Introduction to Mud Witch (0:00 – 0:15)

* **Goal:** Introduce Viviana Matsuda and Mud Witch, establishing a warm, inviting tone.

* **A-Roll & Audio:** Open directly on Viviana's on-camera introduction: “Hi, I'm Viviana matsuda. Um, I do pottery for a living. My brand name is Mud Witch.” [[clip: A001C002_240718OR | 14s-25s]]

* **B-Roll / Transition:** Start with Viviana on camera, then cut to establish the studio space with b-roll of the Mud Witch storefront signage. [[clip: B003C009_240719KG | 16s-20.3s]]

* **Music:** Establish a warm, inviting tone introducing Viviana and her pottery business, set to a continuous bed of upbeat, dreamy background music (dreamy_upbeat.wav). [[sound: 323b9eab-509f-4428-bb58-cc0d4eb72260]]

### Beat 2: Developing Style and Voice (0:15 – 0:30)

* **Goal:** Explore how Viviana found her creative identity and shaped the Mud Witch brand.

* **Interview / Narration:** Viviana narrates her journey of finding her voice and distinctive style for Mud Witch, continuing into her artistic expression. [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 668.9s-682.5s]] [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 682.6s-693.9s]]

* **B-Roll:** Cut to b-roll of the Mud Witch sign displayed on a studio shelf, followed by close details of her ceramics on display. [[clip: B003C028_240719CX | 11.3s-13.6s]] [[clip: B003C011_240719YX | 5.9s-9.1s]]

### Beat 3: Craft and Daily Dedication (0:30 – 0:45)

* **Goal:** Highlight the tactile, meditative craft of pottery and the joy Viviana derives from making pieces by hand.

* **Interview / Voiceover:** Layer interview reflections on her creative process and daily work, speaking to why she loves what she does. [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 702.3s-707.8s]] [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 756s-762s]] [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 892.3s-897.1s]] [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 907.1s-923.6s]]

* **B-Roll / Craft Montage:** Showcase hands-on pottery creation and studio details through active B-roll of throwing clay, shaping forms, and colorful finished mugs. [[clip: B003C006_240719KM | 42.6s-52.4s]] [[clip: B003C007_240719CC | 34.2s-39.8s]] [[clip: B003C050_240719XK | 9.6s-14.2s]]

### Beat 4: Value, Simplicity, and Outro (0:45 – 1:00)

* **Goal:** Conclude with Viviana's core philosophy about keeping life simple and cherishing handmade objects.

* **Interview / Closing Reflection:** Viviana reflects on consumer habits, and concludes with her closing message: “But not only that, but like, you don't need all of that stuff. Like, you could literally just get a couple things that make you happy.” [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 1209.2s-1221.1s]] [[clip: A001C004_240718BC | 1257.6s-1263.8s]]
